content.value_statement: Teams often ship changes without proof that tests catch the intended behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a strict red, green, refactor workflow.
actual_capabilities: Requires a failing test before production code changes.
Guides the red, green, refactor loop for features and bug fixes.
Defines checks for expected test failure and clean passing output.
Explains how to avoid mock-focused tests and test-only production methods.
Provides a completion checklist for test coverage and edge cases.
limitations: Does not provide a test runner or framework integration by itself.
Requires the project to have an existing test setup.
May slow exploratory work when requirements are unclear.
Does not replace human judgment for exceptions or generated code.

use_cases.title: Add a Feature Safely
use_cases.description: Write one failing behavior test, implement only enough code, and refactor after all tests pass.

use_cases.title: Fix a Regression
use_cases.description: Capture the bug with a failing test before changing code, then keep the test as future protection.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Quality
use_cases.description: Review mocks, test-only helpers, and vague assertions against concrete anti-pattern guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Feature with TDD
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill for this feature: [describe feature]. Start with one failing test and explain the expected failure before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Bug with a Test
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a defect fix.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill to fix this bug: [describe bug]. First write a failing reproduction test, then implement the smallest fix.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor with Green Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill while refactoring [area]. Confirm existing tests pass, make small changes, and keep behavior unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for review before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development and testing anti-pattern guidance to review this plan: [paste plan]. Identify missing failing tests and risky mocks.

output_examples.input: Implement retry behavior for failed operations.
output: A first failing test that expects three attempts before success.
A minimal implementation plan that only satisfies that behavior.
A refactor step after the focused test and related tests pass.

output_examples.input: Fix empty email submissions being accepted.
output: A reproduction test showing empty email input returns a validation error.
A small validation change that makes the test pass.
A note to keep edge cases covered before marking the fix complete.

output_examples.input: Review tests that rely heavily on mocks.
output: A list of assertions that test mock behavior instead of product behavior.
Recommendations to use real components or lower-level test doubles.
A simplified test structure that preserves meaningful side effects.

best_practices: Watch each new test fail for the expected reason before writing production code.
Keep each test focused on one observable behavior with a clear name.
Refactor only after the focused test and related tests pass cleanly.
anti_patterns: Writing production code before a failing test exists.
Testing mocks instead of the real behavior users depend on.
Adding methods to production classes only to support tests.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for features, bug fixes, refactors, and behavior changes before writing implementation code.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written as workflow guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the agent to run the project test command when that is appropriate.

faq.question: Does it require a specific test framework?
faq.answer: No. The examples use common JavaScript testing terms, but the workflow applies across frameworks.

faq.question: What if I already wrote the code?
faq.answer: The guidance says to discard or set aside that code and restart from a failing test.

faq.question: How does it help with mocks?
faq.answer: It points to anti-pattern guidance that discourages mock assertions, incomplete mocks, and test-only production APIs.
